skill.name: routeros-firewall
skill.description: Guidance for RouterOS firewall filters, NAT, mangle routing, address lists, interface lists, idempotent rule scripts, DNS redirects, port forwarding, and DoS protection.
skill.summary: Create safer RouterOS firewall, NAT, mangle, and DoS protection guidance.
skill.author: tikoci

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives from markdown code fences, inline RouterOS syntax, sample private IP ranges, and visible MikroTik links. No prompt injection, hidden network access, host command execution, credential handling, or malicious intent was found in the reviewed files.

static_findings.snippet: - `place-before=0` inserts at the top; default `add` appends at the bottom
- An `action=accept` rule must appear BEFORE any `action=drop` for the same traffic
Dynamic entries with `timeout=` expire automatically — the primary pattern for DoS blacklists.
`in-interface-list=` / `out-interface-list=` — powerful RouterOS pattern LLMs never propose. Elimina
**Never use `remove [find dynamic=no]`** — this deletes ALL static rules including those added by ma
`untracked` matches packets explicitly marked via `/ip/firewall/raw action=notrack` — it does NOT ma
L7 alternation: `(a|b|c)` is correct. `(a)|(b)|(c)` has POSIX ERE operator precedence bugs — the mid
| Using `priority=` or rule weight | Rules are sequential — order is position, not weight |
| Writing one rule per IP address | Use `src-address-list=` or `dst-address-list=` |
| `remove [find dynamic=no]` in scripts | Tag-based: `remove [find comment~"prefix-"]` only |
| Forgetting `place-before=` on accept rules | Default appends — accept rules below drops never fire
| `action=log` or `passthrough=yes` stops evaluation | Non-terminal actions continue to next rule —
| `(a)|(b)|(c)` alternation in L7 regexp | Use `(a|b|c)` — grouped form inside one set of parenthese
| One firewall rule per interface | Use `in-interface-list=` with a named interface list |
| IPv6 traffic handled by `/ip/firewall` | IPv6 uses a **separate** `/ipv6/firewall` — rules do not

- `routeros-hotspot` — hotspot chain interaction with firewall, walled garden

content.value_statement: RouterOS firewall syntax is easy to misorder and duplicate. This skill gives focused guidance for filters, NAT, mangle routing, lists, and DoS rules.
actual_capabilities: Explains top-to-bottom RouterOS firewall rule order and first-match behavior.
Shows when to use address lists and interface lists instead of repeated rules.
Guides idempotent rule cleanup with comment prefixes that preserve other rules.
Covers NAT patterns for port forwarding, forced DNS, and WAN masquerade.
Describes mangle routing patterns, DNS exemptions, routing marks, and FastTrack conflicts.
Summarizes DoS patterns using psd, connection-limit, dynamic lists, and tarpit behavior.
limitations: It does not connect to a router or apply configuration changes.
Examples must be adapted to the user network, interfaces, and RouterOS version.
It focuses on IPv4 RouterOS firewall features and notes IPv6 as separate.
It cannot verify live rule counters, packet flow, or device performance.

use_cases.title: Build a Management Access Policy
use_cases.description: Create ordered input-chain guidance that accepts trusted sources before WAN drop rules.

use_cases.title: Design NAT and DNS Controls
use_cases.description: Plan port forwarding, forced DNS redirects, and outbound masquerade without duplicate rules.

use_cases.title: Review Policy Routing Rules
use_cases.description: Check mangle routing marks, DNS exemptions, and FastTrack interactions before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Filter Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for router input protection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a RouterOS input-chain plan for a small office. Include established traffic, trusted management sources, and WAN drop order.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Rules to Lists
prompt_templates.scenario: Reduce repeated IP or interface rules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these firewall requirements and suggest address-list or interface-list patterns. Explain the rule order and cleanup comments.

prompt_templates.title: Plan NAT and DNS Redirects
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare controlled forwarding and DNS handling.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design RouterOS NAT guidance for one web port forward, forced LAN DNS, and WAN masquerade. Mention required user-specific placeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Mangle Routing and DoS Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my RouterOS policy routing and DoS protection plan. Check DNS exemptions, routing marks, FastTrack conflicts, and false positives.

output_examples.input: I need management access only from a trusted LAN and a WAN drop rule.
output_examples.output: Recommended order: allow established traffic first, allow trusted management next, then drop WAN input. Use comments so future cleanup is scoped.

output_examples.input: I have many client IPs and two WAN interfaces.
output: Use an address list for client sources instead of one rule per address.
Use an interface list for WAN roles instead of duplicate interface rules.
Place accept rules before broader drop rules.

output_examples.input: I want policy routing through a VPN for one subnet.
output_examples.output: Create a separate routing table, exempt DNS before marking traffic, then add the marked route disabled until the gateway is ready.

best_practices: Place narrow accept rules before broad drop rules.
Use comment prefixes for idempotent cleanup of owned rules only.
Check FastTrack before adding mangle-based routing marks.
anti_patterns: Do not bulk-remove all static firewall rules.
Do not add one rule per address when an address list fits.
Do not assume IPv4 firewall rules also protect IPv6 traffic.

faq.question: Does this skill apply changes to RouterOS devices?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and example structure only. The user must review and apply changes manually.

faq.question: Can it help with NAT and port forwarding?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers destination NAT, DNS redirect patterns, and outbound masquerade concepts.

faq.question: Does it support mangle policy routing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes routing tables, routing marks, DNS exemptions, and FastTrack interaction notes.

faq.question: Can it validate my live router state?
faq.answer: No. It cannot inspect device counters, installed rules, interface state, or traffic flow.

faq.question: Why does rule order matter?
faq.answer: RouterOS evaluates firewall rules from top to bottom. The first terminal match decides packet handling.

faq.question: Does it cover IPv6 firewall rules?
faq.answer: Only as a warning. RouterOS uses separate IPv6 firewall paths, so IPv6 needs separate rules.
